claim: ACRP Research Report 175 recommends a minimum Speech Transmission Index (STI) of 0.45 for public-address broadcasts in pier-style airport departure lounges.
source_title: ACRP Research Report 175 — Improving Intelligibility of Airport Terminal Public Address Systems, Chapter 3: Speech Intelligibility
supporting_excerpt: This study recommends maintaining an SNR of 10 dB(A) and a minimum STI of 0.45 for public address broadcasts in pier-style departure lounges to ensure that announcements are clearly audible to passengers.
caveat: 0.45 is the minimum for pier-style lounges; other codes cite 0.45 or 0.50 depending on context.

claim: ACRP Research Report 175 states that a good target for announcement levels is a signal-to-noise ratio of 10 to 15 dB above the ambient background noise.
source_title: ACRP Research Report 175 — Improving Intelligibility of Airport Terminal Public Address Systems, Chapter 3
supporting_excerpt: A good target for announcement levels is a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of 10 to 15 dB.
caveat: Higher SNR increases employee and passenger acoustic load; the standard is a target, not a maximum.

claim: ACRP Research Report 175 finds that in airport terminal spaces where ceilings exceed roughly 24 feet, achieving an STI of 0.50 is very challenging.
source_title: ACRP Research Report 175 — Improving Intelligibility of Airport Terminal Public Address Systems, Chapter 4: Physical Factors Affecting PA Intelligibility
page_or_section: Chapter 4 — Physical Factors Affecting PA Intelligibility
supporting_excerpt: Where ceilings are over 24 feet high, it is very challenging to achieve an STI of 0.50.
caveat: Applies to unmodified acoustic geometry; treatment can compensate.

claim: IEC 60268-16:2020 is the international standard defining the Speech Transmission Index (STI) model, test signals, and measurement and prediction methods for objective rating of speech intelligibility.
source_title: IEC 60268-16:2020 — Sound system equipment — Part 16: Objective rating of speech intelligibility by speech transmission index
supporting_excerpt: IEC 60268-16:2020 defines the STI model, test signals, measurement and prediction methods for objective rating of speech intelligibility by speech transmission index.
caveat: Paywalled standard; only publicly summarized scope is quoted.

claim: SFO's Quiet Airport Program reports a 40 percent reduction in announcements at aircraft departure-gate seating areas and estimates that more than 90 minutes of unnecessary announcements per day were eliminated in the International Terminal alone.
source_title: SFO Reduces In-Terminal Noise Levels — Airport X news
supporting_excerpt: A 40 percent reduction in announcements at aircraft departure gate seating areas... more than 90 minutes of unnecessary announcements have been eliminated each day.
units: percent reduction in announcement count; minutes/day
denominator: pre-program announcement baseline at departure-gate seating and International Terminal
caveat: Program-reported figures; not an independently audited measurement. Underlying dB(A) or STI methodology not published.

claim: SFO's Quiet Airport policy has generated documented passenger complaints, including from travelers who report missing flights or finding the reduced-announcement environment confusing.
source_title: Why This Airport's 'Quiet Policy' Is Frustrating Some Passengers — Simple Flying
supporting_excerpt: Passengers can miss their flights if they aren't fully informed about their flight status... making transit less stressful for some can increase the stress for others.
caveat: Trade-press summary; not a systematic passenger survey.

claim: Amsterdam Schiphol publicly describes itself as a silent airport with virtually no announcements, displacing routine flight information to FIDS and the airport app.
source_title: Schiphol in 2025: quieter aircraft, more satisfied travellers and solid financial results — Schiphol newsroom
supporting_excerpt: Schiphol describes itself as a 'Silent Airport' with 'virtually no announcements,' with important information instead shown exclusively on FIDS and the app.
caveat: Operator statement; independent confirmation of announcement volume not provided.

claim: Schiphol reports that the average noise level generated by air traffic in 2025 was approximately 2 decibels lower than in 2018.
source_title: Schiphol in 2025: quieter aircraft, more satisfied travellers and solid financial results
supporting_excerpt: The average noise level generated by air traffic in 2025 was approximately 2 decibels lower than in 2018.
caveat: Air-side noise, not terminal-interior noise; not evidence for terminal PA outcomes.

claim: London City Airport operates a Silent Airport Policy under which public-address announcements are reserved for emergencies.
source_title: Silent Airport Policy — London City Airport
supporting_excerpt: London City Airport operates a silent airport policy. In the case of emergency are announcements made.
caveat: Airport-published policy; excludes airline gate podium announcements which may be handled separately.

claim: NFPA 72 Chapter 24 requires in-building mass notification systems to deliver intelligible audio together with visible notification, including speaker-integrity monitoring, priority messaging hierarchy, specified warning tones, and default emergency sound levels.
source_title: Emergency Communications Systems (ECS) — NFPA 72 Chapter 24, Honeywell/Notifier white paper
supporting_excerpt: NFPA 72 Chapter 24 voice evacuation requirements include the monitoring of speaker integrity, specified warning tones, priority messaging hierarchy, intelligibility, default emergency sound levels and a means for deactivating the fire alarm system.
caveat: Secondary source summarizing NFPA 72; the primary code is paywalled. For final citation, MWAA should reference the current adopted edition of NFPA 72.

claim: Voice-alarm systems used for emergency evacuation broadcasting are certified against EN 54-16 in Europe and UL 2572 in North America.
source_title: Public Address and Voice Alarm Systems (PAVA) — Keenfinity Group / Bosch Building Technologies
supporting_excerpt: A Voice Alarm system adds certified safety features to broadcast clear evacuation messages during emergencies, ensuring compliance with global standards such as EN 54-16 and UL 2572.
caveat: Vendor summary; primary standards (CEN EN 54-16, UL 2572) are paywalled.

claim: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.95 sets a permissible exposure limit of 90 dBA for an 8-hour day and requires a hearing conservation program when employee noise exposures equal or exceed 85 dBA as an 8-hour time-weighted average.
source_title: 29 CFR 1910.95 — Occupational noise exposure — Occupational Safety and Health Administration
supporting_excerpt: OSHA's permissible exposure limit (PEL) is 90 dBA for all workers for an 8 hour day... OSHA requires employers... to implement a hearing conservation program when employee noise exposures equal or exceed 85 decibels (dBA) as an 8-hour time-weighted average.
caveat: Applies to employers of terminal workers; airline gate agent exposure requires airport-specific measurement.

claim: Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport provides assistive T-coil hearing loops in Terminal 4 at gates D11 through D18.
source_title: Special Needs — Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport
supporting_excerpt: Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport offers assistive T-Coil hearing loops in Terminal 4 at gates D11-D18.
caveat: Coverage may have expanded; airport page is the operative reference.

claim: Seattle-Tacoma International Airport has installed hearing-loop induction systems at select ticketing counters, gates, and baggage-claim positions for Alaska, Delta, and JetBlue.
supporting_excerpt: Hearing loop induction systems are available at select locations at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport (SEA), including Alaska Airlines, Delta Air Lines and jetBlue ticketing and service counters, gates and baggage claim.
caveat: Secondary summary; Port of Seattle page should be used for final citation.

claim: Seattle-Tacoma International Airport operates a Sensory Room for neurodivergent travelers and travelers with sensory disabilities, located after security at the A Train Station level.
supporting_excerpt: Seattle-Tacoma International Airport opened a Sensory Room for travelers, including neurodivergent individuals and those with sensory disabilities... has specially selected finishes, lighting, and furniture to create a sense of calm and can be found after security on the A Train Station level.
caveat: Secondary summary; Port of Seattle operator page should be used for final citation.

claim: Indianapolis International Airport has sensory rooms with quiet areas, complimentary comfort items, and private restrooms with adult changing tables and lifts on Concourses A and B, post-security.
supporting_excerpt: Indianapolis International Airport has sensory rooms with quiet areas, complimentary comfort items, and private restrooms with adult changing tables with lifts located post-security on Concourse A and B.

claim: The original Dulles International Airport Main Terminal, designed by Eero Saarinen and completed in 1962, measures approximately 600 feet long and 150 feet wide.
source_title: Dulles International Airport Main Terminal — Wikipedia
supporting_excerpt: The original Dulles International Airport Main Terminal structure, 600 feet long and 150 feet wide, was designed by Eero Saarinen and completed in 1962.
caveat: Wikipedia; primary MWAA / NPS records should be used for a final citation.

claim: Airport Council International — North America has highlighted that data-driven automated announcement platforms enable centralized management, audit logs of every broadcast, and reductions in manual initiation errors that lead to missed calls and missed boardings.
source_title: The Data-Driven Future of Automated Airport Announcements — ACI-NA
supporting_excerpt: Centralized management and analytics platforms allow airports to track, replay, and audit all announcements, identify overuse, and continuously improve passenger flow and information delivery. Targeted, relevant messaging helps reduce stress and minimizes missed flights.
caveat: Industry advocacy piece with vendor context; directional rather than measurement-grade.

claim: In real-world airport terminal seating areas, installed PA systems have been measured with STI values in the 0.32 to 0.42 range, a performance range categorised as 'poor' under IEC 60268-16.
source_title: IEC 60268-16: Sound system equipment — Part 16 — SonaVyx Guide
supporting_excerpt: STI measurements using the installed PA system showed values ranging from 0.32 to 0.42 across the terminal seating areas, categorised as 'poor'.
caveat: Consulting-firm example; specific airport and measurement date not disclosed.
